expectations.text: Output accounts for cohort dilution (15%) and adjusts enrolled sample size upward from the effective sample size
expectations.evidence: With 15% dilution, we need to increase our sample size to account for those who will become unmeasurable: Dilution factor = 1 / (1 - 0.15) = 1 / 0.85 = 1.176; Enrolled per group = 4,278 × 1.176 ≈ 5,035 per group

expectations.text: Output provides enrolled sample per group in the range 4,700–5,500
expectations.evidence: Enrolled per group = 4,278 × 1.176 ≈ 5,035 per group (5,035 falls within the specified range)

expectations.text: Output provides total enrolled sample in the range 9,400–11,000
expectations.evidence: Total enrolled = 2 × 5,035 ≈ 10,070 users (10,070 falls within the specified range)

expectations.text: Output estimates duration in the range 1.8–2.25 weeks using 5,000 new users/week
expectations.evidence: Duration = 10,070 / 5,000 ≈ 2.01 weeks (2.01 weeks falls within the specified range)

expectations.text: Output clarifies that 'eligible traffic' for a retention test means new users entering the cohort, not total active users
expectations.evidence: When designing a retention experiment, 'eligible traffic' refers specifically to new users being enrolled into the cohort, not the total active user base. This is critical because retention is measured from the cohort entry point.
